page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Local storage is bundled with 2880 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions, though it lacks AMX matrix extensions.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several categories. Single-core processing is highly efficient, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and text processing scores all placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core capabilities are strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with large-block read and write bandwidths both reaching the top 10% tier. For software compilation using Clang, the system achieves top-tier performance.

This server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and large-scale data processing. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both demonstrate strong performance in the top 25% tier. While the system handles smaller LLM inference tasks efficiently, performance drops to average levels for larger 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the combination of high memory density, dedicated AMD EPYC cores, and fast bundled NVMe storage provides a balanced resource profile for enterprise databases and memory-cached applications without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware.

This instance is highly suited for large databases, caching layers, and memory-heavy enterprise workloads.
